sense: of a person: at ease, untroubled

terms.gloss: at ease, free from care, untroubled
terms.grammar: adjective: with dē and the ablative of what one need not worry about
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.52.2: dē linguā Latīnā sēcūrī es animī
terms.comment: From sē-, without, and cūra: free of worry (Lewis & Short). Of a place, “safe” only after Augustus and rarely (the classical word is tūtus); “careless, heedless” is post-Augustan and very rare (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: phrase: the person in the dative
terms.comment: The everyday way to say one is well off where one is (see I’m having a lovely time).

terms.grammar: phrase: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum with aequō animō and an object or accusative and infinitive
evidence: Ter. And. 397: sed sī tē aequō animō ferre accipiet
terms.comment: To bear something with an even mind: the Latin for being at ease with a situation (see calmly). The opposite is molestē ferre, to be upset by it.

phrases.latin: dē linguā Latīnā sēcūrī es animī.
phrases.english: As for the Latin, don’t worry about it.

phrases.latin: sī tēcum mihi, cāre Mārtiālis, sēcūrīs liceat fruī diēbus
phrases.english: if I could enjoy carefree days with you, dear Martial
